A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ASSESS/TransTED study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable, allowing retained material to be matched across revisions and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original evaluations on 524 expert-annotated EPLA pairs, including baseline comparisons, a transformation ablation, threshold analysis, and qualitative cases.

after.justification: V2 reports evaluations on 1,247 annotated pairs, together with original execution-time measurements, tactic-usage analyses, and additional failure cases.

M1.justification: The core OPT/TransTED framework remains. Algorithm 1 replaces norm_num1 preprocessing and the rfl completion check with exact?, and adds node-limit stopping. Table 1 changes the implication-congruence tactic from try exact? to try rfl. These are local procedural changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Lean 4 statement similarity using miniF2F-test and ProofNet-test. The additional generated pairs and translator configurations enlarge evaluation within the same mathematical domains and task requirements.

E2.justification: Typecheck is removed from the main and detailed baseline comparisons. Figure 3 adds TED Similarity to the threshold comparison previously containing BLEU and TransTED Similarity. The remaining main comparator methods are retained.

E3.justification: Table 2 expands EPLA-miniF2F from 373 to 831 pairs and EPLA-ProofNet from 151 to 416, adding Goedel-Formalizer-V2-8B and Qwen3-Max generators. The annotation panel increases from five to seven experts. Majority Voting changes from DeepSeek-V3.1 to DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp, and execution time becomes an additional evaluation measure. These substantially extend settings within the retained tasks.

E4.justification: V2 adds quantitative tactic-usage and adoption analyses in Figures 4–6, TransTED false-negative and false-positive cases in Appendix B, and an expanded baseline-error taxonomy covering BEq in Appendix F.4. The existing transformation ablation and successful examples are retained, while threshold analysis gains the TED comparison.

E5.justification: Neither version reports independent repeated-run variability, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The 16-round majority-voting procedure remains unchanged in count. New tactic frequencies and average execution times do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 3 replaces the aggregate results: TransTED accuracy/Kappa changes from 78.82%/0.46 to 70.16%/0.35 on EPLA-miniF2F and from 70.86%/0.40 to 67.31%/0.30 on EPLA-ProofNet. Changed samples and settings prevent interpreting these as same-setting performance losses. V2 also adds runtimes, tactic counts, and BEq false positives, including four miniF2F cases and one ProofNet case.

T1.justification: Definition 1 and Theorem 1 replace extended-real codomains with finite nonnegative reals; Appendix C adds an explicit finite-bound argument. The disconnected-path convention is removed. V2 also removes the assertion that normalized TED Similarity lies in [0,1], retaining the formula and the negative-valued example. The central maximum-pseudometric theorem remains.

C1.justification: The central claims about operator-tree evaluation, semantic transformations, and leading accuracy/Kappa are retained. EPLA's contribution is updated to 1,247 pairs, while v1's claims that it is the first large-scale and largest benchmark are withdrawn. The introduction also drops the explicit comparative efficiency claim against LLM judges while retaining reproducibility claims.

C2.justification: V1 argues that threshold stability avoids dataset-specific optimization; v2 Appendix F.1 explicitly recommends domain-specific calibration, explaining thresholds of 0.61 versus 0.38 through structural diversity. Appendix B adds substantive limitations concerning restricted tactics and structurally similar false positives, and argues for debugging applications. V2 also develops explanations of tactic specialization and baseline failure mechanisms.

D1.justification: V1 promises a future release; v2 reports a repository containing code, data, and results. V2 newly specifies hardware, BEq's tactic list and generation budget, top-5 rw? suggestions, a 32-node limit, and a ten-minute timeout. It also adds autoformalization prompts and explicit benchmark-field and label documentation. These disclosures substantially improve reproducibility information without establishing that every newly documented setting changed.

R1.justification: V2 adds explicit positioning against GTED, acknowledging its prior use of operator trees and distinguishing ASSESS through proof-based transformations and pseudometric formalization. It also adds references for newer formalization/model work and updates the DeepSeek reference. The broader related-work organization remains stable.

P1.justification: The abstract and numerous introduction, methodology, and results passages are rewritten. The appendices are substantially reorganized: proofs and pseudocode move, benchmark-label explanations receive a dedicated section, and prompts are integrated into experimental details. Reproducibility, limitations, acknowledgements, and writing-assistance sections are added.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is comprehensively redrawn with concrete examples and a search-tree illustration. Figure 3 gains a TED curve and marked optimal thresholds; Figures 4–6 introduce tactic visualizations. Benchmark and detailed-results tables gain columns, including execution times, and new annotation and error-classification tables structure the appendices.

improvement.justification: V2 improves assessability through explicit reproduction settings, reported resource access, measured computational costs, and failure and threshold-calibration analyses missing from v1. Evaluation across additional formalizers also strengthens the evidence within the existing tasks. These benefits are tempered by new inconsistencies: Algorithm 1 adds node-limit stopping without handling it in the non-proof return branch, and Appendix B claims 100% BEq precision despite the false positives reported in Table 3 and Appendix F.4. The net improvement is therefore limited.
